title: Cheap Firehall Meals That Still Taste Good
subtitle: Stretch the grocery budget without crew complaints
description: Pasta, chili, tacos, egg bakes, and chicken thighs that taste good on a tight budget — flavor from technique, not price tags.
intro: Budget nights are normal — dues, fundraisers, and 'we already spent too much this month' happen. Cheap firehall meals lean on pasta, beans, chicken thighs, ground beef, and eggs. Flavor comes from browning, acid, and salt — not expensive cuts.

sections.heading: Cheap does not mean bland
paragraphs: Toast spices, brown meat, finish with lemon or vinegar. Crews notice technique more than truffle oil.

sections.heading: Shop smart for the hall
paragraphs: Buy in bulk for staples, thighs over breasts when appropriate, and one 'splurge' topping so budget night still feels intentional.

practicalAdvice: Buy whole birds or thighs instead of breasts when appropriate.
Beans and lentils stretch chili without complaint if seasoned boldly.
Frozen veg and bulk rice are hall allies.

faqs.question: Where do these recipes come from?
faqs.answer: Each link goes to a full recipe on Firehall Meals — crew-sized portions, station timing, and steps written for a shared kitchen. Not home-blog scaling.

faqs.question: What if crew size or time changes tonight?
faqs.answer: Use Find a Meal with your headcount and minutes available. It pulls from the same hall-tested dinners these guides recommend.
